subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: GPU types & TPS targets
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Jordan Lloyd <jordan.lloyd@acme-pay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.inference>
Date: 2025-11-10T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: GPU types & TPS targets

Jordan — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap + a few follow-ups so we can size Dedicated for Acme:  

- High-level ask: predictable, low-latency inference for fraud-detection assistant + conversational payments UI. You indicated Dedicated capacity is preferred over Hosted because of data isolation and predictable throughput.
- Questions we still need answered to map to a Dedicated configuration:
  1) Preferred GPU family (you mentioned A100/80GB vs H100) — any hard requirement?
  2) Sustained and peak request targets (RPS/TPS) and expected concurrency.
  3) Typical token mix: average prompt length, average generated tokens, % of short queries vs long-form.
  4) Streaming vs non-streaming percentage and any strict latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99).

Action items: if you can reply with the numbers below today/tomorrow we can turn around a sizing worksheet + ballpark pricing for Dedicated. I attached a one-page sizing CSV template (acme-dedicated-sizing.csv) to make this quick. Also happy to schedule a 30-min infra deep-dive next week with our infra engineer.

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme-dedicated-sizing.csv (CSV, 2KB)
From: Jordan Lloyd <jordan.lloyd@acme-pay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: 2025-11-11T09:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: GPU types & TPS targets

Thanks Marissa — good call. Answers below (I've copied Priya who runs infra at Acme):

1) GPU preference: We prefer A100-80GB for compatibility with our current stacks; H100 would be ok if performance/cost favors it but A100 is the safer baseline.

2) Traffic targets:
   - Sustained: 60 requests/sec (RPS) during business hours
   - Peak: ~120 RPS for ~10 minutes during promotions
   - Concurrency target: 40-50 concurrent active sessions (these are streaming chat sessions that keep a connection open)

3) Token mix (estimates):
   - Average prompt tokens: 250
   - Average completion tokens: 600
   - Distribution: ~70% short queries (<=256 total tokens), ~30% long-form (1k-2k tokens)

4) Streaming: ~75% of conversations use streaming responses. Latency SLOs: p50 < 200ms for short responses, p95 < 700ms. p99 we can tolerate up to 1.5s.

Other notes: we will need VPC peering for private networking into our AWS account — Dedicated with VPC peering is ideal. Priya, feel free to add details.

—Jordan
Jordan Lloyd
Senior Product Manager, Acme Payments
jordan.lloyd@acme-pay.com

Marissa — forwarding Jordan's reply. Key numbers look actionable. A couple internal asks before we propose a config:  

- Can you confirm whether the "requests" Jordan called out are single-turn text generation requests or multi-turn chat sessions that keep the KV cache warm? My read is mostly chat (streaming), so effective tokens/sec per session will be higher.
- We should map to candidate pod sizes: A100-80GB x N GPUs vs H100 x M GPUs vs mixed for fallbacks. Please fill the sizing CSV with expected percent traffic per model and baseline model (Llama2-70B vs Llama2-13B or other).
- I'll loop infra for estimated costs and GPU availability in us-west-2.

If you want, I can draft 2 sizing options (cost-optimized and low-latency) once we have the token mix per model.

-Marcus
Director, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Jordan Lloyd <jordan.lloyd@acme-pay.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@acme-pay.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference>
Date: 2025-11-12T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: GPU types & TPS targets

Jordan / Priya — thanks for the detailed numbers, that is super helpful. I filled out the sizing worksheet and attached a short proposal with two candidate configurations:  

1) Low-latency config (recommended if p95/p99 are critical):
   - Hardware: A100-80GB (N=6 GPUs) across 2 pods for HA
   - Expected sustained capacity: ~70 RPS, burst to 140 RPS with autoscale buffer
   - Concurrency target: supports ~60 streaming sessions with ~700 gen tokens avg
   - Estimated monthly cost (infra only): $XX,XXX (ballpark)

2) Cost-optimized config:
   - Hardware: A10G + A100 mix (A10G for short/embedding-heavy paths, A100 for long-form)
   - Expected sustained capacity: ~65 RPS, bursts to 120 RPS
   - Concurrency: ~45 streaming sessions
   - Estimated monthly cost (infra only): ~$YY,YYY (ballpark)

Notes and assumptions (included in attached CSV): token averages as you provided, 75% streaming, model mix assumed Llama2-13B for majority of short queries and a 70B variant for long-form generation. If you prefer H100 pricing/perf, we can swap and re-run estimates.

Attachments: acme-dedicated-sizing.csv (filled), acme-capacity-proposal.pdf (2 pages)

Next steps:
- Quick infra deep-dive with Marcus and our infra engineer (propose Fri 11/14 10:00-10:30 PT).
- I will open a HubSpot quote for the two configs and a tentative timeline for provisioning.
- Please confirm which config to move to a formal quote.

Thanks — Marissa

- We want to prioritize low-latency for the payments assistant (p95 < 700ms). Let's proceed with the Low-latency config as the primary.
- Confirm A100-80GB is fine. H100 is optional for a future perf run.
- We'll need VPC peering and a short SOC2 evidence pass (Priya will follow up on the compliance docs).
